fichas.title: Two-skin party walls
fichas.summary: A two-skin party wall uses a separating joint extending through the full depth of the houses. The cavity is filled with gapless, full-surface fibre insulating boards without sound bridges. Special boards are required for in-situ concrete skins under high concreting loads. For sufficiently heavy skins, boards may be omitted if construction measures prevent sound bridges. The continuous joint is stated to improve weighted sound reduction compared with a two-skin wall without sound bridges.
uses: Separate adjoining houses while limiting airborne sound transmission
Reduce sound bridges between wall skins
furniture_equipment: Timber guides, removed after wall construction

fichas.title: Impact sound insulation of floors
fichas.summary: Impact sound results from direct vibration of a floor slab. A floating screed over a gapless, soft springy insulation layer is the usual construction; a protective layer covers the insulation. The screed edge must allow free movement and be sealed with permanently elastic jointing material to avoid sound bridges. Soft springy floor coverings or suspended soft ceilings are alternatives in specified slab conditions. Illustrated examples include solid, vaulted and timber-joist floors, with sound-insulation performance figures and references to page 478.
uses: Reduce impact sound transmission to the room below
Provide impact sound insulation using floating screeds, resilient floor coverings, or suspended ceilings
